source.title: Optimization as a Dynamical System: Generative Schedules from Latent ODEs

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the general idea that flatter minima indicate better generalization and measures loss sharpness across learning-rate schedules. It does not test any listed claim version: it does not study random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected models, the specified optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness versus the training–test gap, or removal of memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy comparisons for its proposed learning-rate scheduler and baselines, but those results evaluate the scheduling method, not the listed claims about memorization, training–test gaps, or their specified causes. The sharpness measurements in Table 2 are retained as a related finding under fits_no_version. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima favor generalization to interpret its scheduler's performance. Its own comparisons evaluate learning-rate schedules, not any listed version. In particular, largest Hessian eigenvalue and test accuracy do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness versus training–test error gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report superior test accuracy across the five tested model–dataset pairs and lower Hessian sharpness for ResNet18 on CIFAR-100. They interpret the flatter minima as explaining improved generalization; a magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship is not established.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains neural networks with a generative learning-rate scheduler and measures test accuracy and largest Hessian eigenvalue; it does not apply the original methods in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured sharpness differs by learning-rate schedule in the ResNet18–CIFAR-100 comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet18 on CIFAR-100, LODE has the lowest reported largest Hessian eigenvalue: 0.62 ± 0.22 versus 1.22–13.23 for the compared schedules. Table 1 also reports the highest test accuracy for LODE, but neither result establishes the V7 gap relationship.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedules can differ in final Hessian sharpness and held-out accuracy; in this ResNet18–CIFAR-100 comparison, LODE achieves both the lowest reported largest Hessian eigenvalue and the highest test accuracy.

record.problems: The sharpness comparison is reported for one model–dataset pair and uses largest Hessian eigenvalue rather than the magnitude-aware measure in V7. The paper does not report the training–test gap for this comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Test-accuracy results in Table 1 and other scheduler-performance results were left out because they evaluate the proposed scheduling method rather than a listed claim version or a measured training–test gap.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting random labels and generalizing on natural labels.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No matched adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison: optimizers differ across workloads, while the within-workload experiments compare schedules.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
Dropout is used in architectures but is not varied or removed in a controlled comparison.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure, training–test error-gap comparison among similarly fitted networks, or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All seven extracted numerical values agree with Table 2. The scheduler-performance results omitted by the record do not supply a test of another listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance are not studied.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Optimizer comparisons in this paper are not the specified adaptive-versus-SGD generalization test.
Dropout is specified in architectures, but its effect is not compared.
The paper measures largest Hessian eigenvalue, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or the training–test gap, and does not compare the specified norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.
